A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAC research work. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-F are readable and matchable despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments, backbone comparisons, training-time measurements and parameter studies in Section 5, with additional yearly results and noise analysis in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including EAC forecasting scores across three datasets.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same node-level prompt pool, element-wise input fusion, frozen backbone during continual adaptation, prompt expansion and low-rank compression. No algorithmic component or training procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PEMS-Stream traffic flow, Air-Stream air quality and Energy-Stream turbine measurements over the same periods. The limited-data PEMS-Stream scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same classical training schemes, TrafficStream, STKEC, LoRA, and reported PECPM/TFMoE and ST-CRL results. Main Tables 1 and 2 exchange numbers without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: The 6:2:2 splits, 12-step input, forecasting horizons, MAE/RMSE/MAPE metrics, 20% limited-data setting and backbone configurations remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same training budget, batch size and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Both retain the heterogeneity and spectral diagnostics, few-shot tests, backbone comparisons, efficiency study, rank sensitivity analysis and Appendix D noise analysis. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify five experiment repetitions with means and standard deviations in Section 5.1 and five random runs for Appendix D results. Uncertainty reporting practices and statistical procedures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched table values and figure contents are unchanged, including yearly appendix results. For example, EAC's PEMS-Stream average MAE remains 13.53±0.06 and RMSE 21.77±0.10 in v2 Table 1 and v3 Table 2.

T1.justification: The definitions, two propositions, Appendix A proofs and Appendix E formulas are retained. Removing the equation number beside Proposition 1 and renumbering subsequent equations do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same expand-and-compress contribution and claims of effectiveness, efficiency, universality, simplicity and lightweight adaptation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of forecasting performance, heterogeneity, compression and efficiency are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same discussion of historical-data costs and limitations concerning graph contraction, the seven-year evaluation span and parameter inflation.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly labels the existing EAC repository 'Fully Open Source'; v2 only states that the repository is available. This is a limited disclosure change, not evidence of a new release. Implementation details, preprocessing, hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to continual learning, prompt learning and spatio-temporal forecasting remain the same. Bibliography and citation-style changes do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes front-page metadata into repository, publication, correspondence and date fields, renames 'Supplementary Material' to 'Appendix', and makes small heading and punctuation edits. The substantive prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the document with a shaded title/abstract block, different typography and margins, restyled captions, more spacious tables and relocated floats. Appendix tables and figures receive section-based numbering, and appendix pages gain return-to-index links. The underlying figure graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The more spacious result tables and working appendix-index return links make the retained evidence easier to read and navigate. These are limited usability gains: the method, experiments, results, proofs and limitations remain unchanged.
